<details class="result-group" id="definition-10-1" open>
<summary><span>Definition 10.1</span><span class="result-count">1 endpoint</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>Bootstrap convergence in probability: <code>P*[‖Z*_n − Z‖ &gt; ε] →p 0</code> for all ε &gt; 0</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-tendstoinbootstrapprobability">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">def</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.TendstoInBootstrapProbability</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Definition 10.1: convergence in bootstrap probability.</p>
<p><code>Zstar n -&gt;p* Z</code> means that for every positive tolerance <code>η</code>, the conditional
tail probability <code>Pstar[dist (Zstar n) Z ≥ η]</code> converges to zero in ordinary
probability under the original-sample law <code>μ</code>.</p>
<p>The inequality is written with <code>≤</code> to match Mathlib's <code>TendstoInMeasure</code>
convention; this is the usual harmless closed-tail version of convergence in
probability. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">{Ω : Type u_1} →
  {Ωs : Type u_2} →
    {E : Type u_3} →
      {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} →
        {mΩs : MeasurableSpace Ωs} →
          [PseudoMetricSpace E] →
            MeasureTheory.Measure Ω → (Nat → Ω → MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs) → (Nat → Ω → Ωs → E) → (Ω → E) → Prop</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/BootstrapUtils.lean#L65">HansenEconometrics/BootstrapUtils.lean:65</a></p>
</div>
</details>
</div>
</details>

<div class="textbook-statement"><p>For the sample mean, the leave-one-out mean can be written in terms of the full-sample mean and the omitted observation; averaging the leave-one-out means recovers the full-sample mean, and each leave-one-out deviation is <code>(Ybar - Y_i)/(n-1)</code></p></div>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-jackknifeleaveoneoutmean-eq">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.jackknifeLeaveOneOutMean_eq</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen equation (10.2): the leave-one-out mean written in terms of the
full-sample mean and the deleted observation. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {E : Type u_4} {ι : Type u_7} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : DecidableEq ι] [Nontrivial ι]
  [inst_3 : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_4 : NormedSpace Real E] (Y : ι → E) (i : ι),

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/Chapter10Bootstrap/Empirical.lean#L130">HansenEconometrics/Chapter10Bootstrap/Empirical.lean:130</a></p>

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen's displayed identity after (10.2): each leave-one-out mean differs

<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>

<details class="result-group" id="equation-10-3">
<summary><span>Equation 10.3</span><span class="result-count">1 endpoint</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>The sample-mean jackknife covariance estimator reduces exactly to the conventional covariance estimator for the variance of the mean</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-jackknifecovariance-leaveoneoutmean-eq-samplemeancovariance">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.jackknifeCovariance_leaveOneOutMean_eq_sampleMeanCovariance</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen equation (10.3): for the sample mean, Tukey's jackknife covariance
equals the conventional covariance estimator for the variance of the mean. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {ι : Type u_7} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : DecidableEq ι] [Nontrivial ι] {k : Type u_8} [inst_3 : Fintype k]
  (Y : ι → k → Real),
  Eq (HansenEconometrics.jackknifeCovariance fun i =&gt; HansenEconometrics.jackknifeLeaveOneOutMean Y i) fun a b =&gt;
    instHMul.hMul
      (instHMul.hMul (Real.instInv.inv (Fintype.card ι).cast)
        (Real.instInv.inv (instHSub.hSub (Fintype.card ι).cast 1)))
      (Finset.univ.sum fun i =&gt;
        instHMul.hMul (instHSub.hSub (HansenEconometrics.empiricalMean Y a) (Y i a))
          (instHSub.hSub (HansenEconometrics.empiricalMean Y b) (Y i b)))</code></pre>
</details>
<details class="dependency-list"><summary>Direct statement dependencies (3)</summary><ul><li><code>HansenEconometrics.empiricalMean</code></li><li><code>HansenEconometrics.jackknifeCovariance</code></li><li><code>HansenEconometrics.jackknifeLeaveOneOutMean</code></li></ul></details>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-leaveoneoutbeta-eq-olsbeta-sub-invgram-mulvec">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.leaveOneOutBeta_eq_olsBeta_sub_invGram_mulVec</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 3.7 / equation (3.43): leave-one-out coefficients can be
computed from the full-sample coefficient and prediction error. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype n] [inst_1 : Fintype k] [inst_2 : DecidableEq k] (X : Matrix n k Real)
  (y : n → Real) (i : n) [inst_3 : Invertible (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul X.transpose X)]
  [inst_4 : Invertible (HansenEconometrics.leaveOneOutGram X i)],
  Eq (HansenEconometrics.leaveOneOutBeta X y i)
    (instHSub.hSub (HansenEconometrics.olsBeta X y)
      (instHSMul.hSMul (HansenEconometrics.leaveOneOutResidual X y i)
        ((inst_3.invOf (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul X.transpose X)).mulVec (X i))))</code></pre>
</details>

</div>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-leaveoneoutresidual-eq-inv-one-sub-leverage-mul-residual">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.leaveOneOutResidual_eq_inv_one_sub_leverage_mul_residual</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 3.7 / equation (3.44): leave-one-out prediction errors are
full-sample residuals scaled by <code>(1 - hᵢᵢ)⁻¹</code>. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype n] [inst_1 : Fintype k] [inst_2 : DecidableEq k] (X : Matrix n k Real)
  (y : n → Real) (i : n) [inst_3 : Invertible (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul X.transpose X)]
  [inst_4 : Invertible (HansenEconometrics.leaveOneOutGram X i)],
  Ne (instHSub.hSub 1 (HansenEconometrics.leverageValue X i)) 0 →
    Eq (HansenEconometrics.leaveOneOutResidual X y i)
      (instHMul.hMul (Real.instInv.inv (instHSub.hSub 1 (HansenEconometrics.leverageValue X i)))
        (HansenEconometrics.residual X y i))</code></pre>
</details>
<details class="dependency-list"><summary>Direct statement dependencies (4)</summary><ul><li><code>HansenEconometrics.leaveOneOutGram</code></li><li><code>HansenEconometrics.leaveOneOutResidual</code></li><li><code>HansenEconometrics.leverageValue</code></li><li><code>HansenEconometrics.residual</code></li></ul></details>

</div>
</details>

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen equation (3.48): the change in coefficient estimates after dropping
observation <code>i</code>. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype n] [inst_1 : Fintype k] [inst_2 : DecidableEq k] (X : Matrix n k Real)
  (y : n → Real) (i : n) [inst_3 : Invertible (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul X.transpose X)]

<details class="result-group" id="equation-10-5">
<summary><span>Equation 10.5</span><span class="result-count">6 of 7 linked endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>The OLS leave-one-out jackknife covariance equals the HC3 covariance estimator minus the finite-sample mean-adjustment outer product</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-jackknifecovariance-leaveoneoutbeta-eq-hc3-sub-meanadjustment">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.jackknifeCovariance_leaveOneOutBeta_eq_HC3_sub_meanAdjustment</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen equation (10.5): the OLS leave-one-out jackknife covariance equals
the HC3 covariance estimator less the finite-sample mean-adjustment outer
product. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {ι : Type u_7} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : DecidableEq ι] [Nontrivial ι] {k : Type u_8} [inst_3 : Fintype k]
  [inst_4 : DecidableEq k] (X : Matrix ι k Real) (y : ι → Real)
  [inst_5 : Invertible (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul X.transpose X)]
  (hloo : (i : ι) → Invertible (HansenEconometrics.leaveOneOutGram X i)),
  (∀ (i : ι), Ne (instHSub.hSub 1 (HansenEconometrics.leverageValue X i)) 0) →
    Eq (HansenEconometrics.jackknifeCovariance (HansenEconometrics.olsLeaveOneOutBetaFamily X y hloo))
      (instHSub.hSub
        (instHSMul.hSMul (instHDiv.hDiv (instHSub.hSub (Fintype.card ι).cast 1) (Fintype.card ι).cast)
          (HansenEconometrics.olsHuberWhiteHC3VarianceEstimator X y))
        (instHSMul.hSMul (instHSub.hSub (Fintype.card ι).cast 1)
          (Matrix.vecMulVec (HansenEconometrics.empiricalMean (HansenEconometrics.olsLeaveOneOutInfluence X y hloo))

<div class="declaration-body">

<p>The cluster-deleted coefficient equals the full-sample coefficient minus the
cluster leverage correction based on the CR3-style prediction errors. </p></div>

<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype n] [inst_1 : Fintype k] [inst_2 : DecidableEq k] {G : Type u_3}

<details class="result-group" id="equation-10-6">
<summary><span>Equation 10.6</span><span class="result-count">3 endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>The probability that a fixed observation appears at least once in an <code>n</code>-draw bootstrap sample is <code>1 - (1 - 1/n)^n</code>, with limit <code>1 - e^{-1}</code></p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-bootstrapobservationinclusionprobability">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">def</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.bootstrapObservationInclusionProbability</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen equation (10.6): displayed probability that one fixed observation is
included at least once in an <code>n</code>-draw bootstrap sample from <code>n</code> observations.</p>
<p>The expression is totalized at <code>n = 0</code>; the asymptotic result below is the
textbook statement. </p></div>

wrapper applies. </p></div>

  {Pstar : Nat → Ω → MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs} {Tstar : Nat → Ω → Ωs → Real} {a : Nat → Real},
  (∀ (n : Nat), Real.instLT.lt 0 (a n)) →
    ∀ {θ : Real} {θhat : Nat → Ω → Real} {ξ : Ωlim → Real} {q α : Real},
      MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution (fun n ω =&gt; instHMul.hMul (a n) (instHSub.hSub (θhat n ω) θ)) Filter.atTop ξ
          (fun x =&gt; μ) ν →

          (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω),

                  Real.instLE.le (instHDiv.hDiv α 2)
                    (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapScalarCDF Pstar Tstar x n ω)).Nonempty) →
            (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω),
                BddBelow
                  (setOf fun x =&gt;
                    Real.instLE.le (instHDiv.hDiv α 2) (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapScalarCDF Pstar Tstar x n ω))) →
              (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω) (x : Real),
                  Real.instLT.lt (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapScalarCDF Pstar Tstar x n ω) (instHDiv.hDiv α 2) →
                    Exists fun δ =&gt;
                      And (Real.instLT.lt 0 δ)
                        (Real.instLT.lt (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapScalarCDF Pstar Tstar (instHAdd.hAdd x δ) n ω)
                          (instHDiv.hDiv α 2))) →
                (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω),
                    (setOf fun x =&gt;
                        Real.instLE.le (instHSub.hSub 1 (instHDiv.hDiv α 2))
                          (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapScalarCDF Pstar Tstar x n ω)).Nonempty) →
                  (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω),

                            And (Real.instLT.lt 0 δ)
                              (Real.instLT.lt
                                (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapScalarCDF Pstar Tstar (instHAdd.hAdd x δ) n ω)
                                (instHSub.hSub 1 (instHDiv.hDiv α 2)))) →
                      (StrictMono fun x =&gt; (ProbabilityTheory.cdf η).toFun x) →
                        (∀ (x : Real),

<details class="result-group" id="equation-10-11">
<summary><span>Equation 10.11</span><span class="result-count">6 of 7 linked endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>The covariance of one bootstrap observation drawn uniformly from the empirical support equals the empirical covariance matrix</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-covmat-uniformon-univ-eq-card-inv-smul-sum-centered">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.covMat_uniformOn_univ_eq_card_inv_smul_sum_centered</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Finite-dimensional empirical covariance identity for one bootstrap draw.</p>
<p>This is the matrix form of Hansen's exact bootstrap covariance formula
(10.11): under uniform resampling from a finite empirical support, the
covariance matrix is the average outer product of deviations from the empirical
mean. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {ι : Type u_7} [inst : MeasurableSpace ι] [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [MeasurableSingletonClass ι] {k : Type u_8}
  (Y : ι → k → Real),
  Eq (HansenEconometrics.covMat (ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn Set.univ) Y) fun a b =&gt;
    instHSMul.hSMul (ENNReal.instInv.inv (Fintype.card ι).cast).toReal
      (Finset.univ.sum fun i =&gt;
        instHMul.hMul
          (instHSub.hSub (Y i a)
            (instHSMul.hSMul (ENNReal.instInv.inv (Fintype.card ι).cast).toReal (Finset.univ.sum fun j =&gt; Y j a)))
          (instHSub.hSub (Y i b)
            (instHSMul.hSMul (ENNReal.instInv.inv (Fintype.card ι).cast).toReal (Finset.univ.sum fun j =&gt; Y j b))))</code></pre>
</details>
<details class="dependency-list"><summary>Direct statement dependencies (1)</summary><ul><li><code>HansenEconometrics.covMat</code></li></ul></details>
<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/Chapter10Bootstrap/Empirical.lean#L6147">HansenEconometrics/Chapter10Bootstrap/Empirical.lean:6147</a></p>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-variance-uniformon-univ-eq-card-inv-smul-sum-sq-centered">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.variance_uniformOn_univ_eq_card_inv_smul_sum_sq_centered</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Scalar empirical variance identity for one bootstrap draw.</p>
<p>This is the scalar version of Hansen's exact bootstrap covariance formula
(10.11): under uniform resampling from a finite empirical support, the
variance is the average squared deviation from the empirical mean. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {ι : Type u_7} [inst : MeasurableSpace ι] [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [MeasurableSingletonClass ι] (Y : ι → Real),
  Eq (ProbabilityTheory.variance Y (ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn Set.univ))
    (instHSMul.hSMul (ENNReal.instInv.inv (Fintype.card ι).cast).toReal
      (Finset.univ.sum fun i =&gt;
        instHPow.hPow
          (instHSub.hSub (Y i)
            (instHSMul.hSMul (ENNReal.instInv.inv (Fintype.card ι).cast).toReal (Finset.univ.sum fun j =&gt; Y j)))
          2))</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/Chapter10Bootstrap/Empirical.lean#L4570">HansenEconometrics/Chapter10Bootstrap/Empirical.lean:4570</a></p>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-taylor-charfun-centered-standardized-uniformon-univ">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.taylor_charFun_centered_standardized_uniformOn_univ</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Taylor expansion at zero for the standardized centered empirical one-draw
characteristic function.</p>
<p>This packages Mathlib's second-order characteristic-function Taylor lemma with
the finite empirical mean-zero and variance identities. It is the local analytic
input used by the characteristic-function proof of Hansen Theorem 10.4. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {ι : Type u_7} [inst : MeasurableSpace ι] [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [MeasurableSingletonClass ι] [Nonempty ι]
  (Y : ι → Real),
  Ne (ProbabilityTheory.variance Y (ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn Set.univ)) 0 →
    Asymptotics.IsLittleO (nhds 0)
      (fun t =&gt;
        instHSub.hSub
          (MeasureTheory.charFun
            (MeasureTheory.Measure.map
              (fun i =&gt;
                instHDiv.hDiv (instHSub.hSub (Y i) (HansenEconometrics.empiricalMean Y))
                  (ProbabilityTheory.variance Y (ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn Set.univ)).sqrt)
              (ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn Set.univ))
            t)
          (instHSub.hSub 1 (instHDiv.hDiv (instHPow.hPow (Complex.ofReal t) 2) 2)))
      fun t =&gt; instHPow.hPow t 2</code></pre>
</details>
<details class="dependency-list"><summary>Direct statement dependencies (1)</summary><ul><li><code>HansenEconometrics.empiricalMean</code></li></ul></details>

</div>
</details>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-integral-sq-sub-empiricalmean-uniformon-univ-eq-variance">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.integral_sq_sub_empiricalMean_uniformOn_univ_eq_variance</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Raw second moment of a centered empirical one-draw statistic.</p>
<p>Since the centered empirical one-draw statistic has exact mean zero, its raw
second moment is the empirical one-draw variance. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {ι : Type u_7} [inst : MeasurableSpace ι] [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [MeasurableSingletonClass ι] (Y : ι → Real),
  Eq
    (MeasureTheory.integral (ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn Set.univ) fun i =&gt;
      instHPow.hPow (instHSub.hSub (Y i) (HansenEconometrics.empiricalMean Y)) 2)
    (ProbabilityTheory.variance Y (ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn Set.univ))</code></pre>
</details>
<details class="dependency-list"><summary>Direct statement dependencies (1)</summary><ul><li><code>HansenEconometrics.empiricalMean</code></li></ul></details>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-charfun-centered-uniformon-univ-inv-sqrt-succ-pow-tendsto">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.charFun_centered_uniformOn_univ_inv_sqrt_succ_pow_tendsto</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Gaussian characteristic-function power limit for a centered empirical
one-draw law with fixed support.</p>
<p>This removes the standardization from
<code>charFun_centered_standardized_uniformOn_univ_inv_sqrt_succ_pow_tendsto</code>: the
fixed-support limit has the empirical one-draw variance as its Gaussian scale. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {ι : Type u_7} [inst : MeasurableSpace ι] [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [MeasurableSingletonClass ι] [Nonempty ι]
  (Y : ι → Real),
  Ne (ProbabilityTheory.variance Y (ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn Set.univ)) 0 →
    ∀ (t : Real),
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun n =&gt;
          instHPow.hPow
            (MeasureTheory.charFun
              (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun i =&gt; instHSub.hSub (Y i) (HansenEconometrics.empiricalMean Y))
                (ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn Set.univ))
              (instHMul.hMul (Real.instInv.inv (instHAdd.hAdd n.cast 1).sqrt) t))
            n.succ)
        Filter.atTop
        (nhds
          (Complex.exp
            (instHDiv.hDiv
              (Complex.instNeg.neg
                (instHPow.hPow
                  (Complex.ofReal
                    (instHMul.hMul (ProbabilityTheory.variance Y (ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn Set.univ)).sqrt t))
                  2))
              2)))</code></pre>
</details>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-charfun-centered-standardized-uniformon-univ-inv-sqrt-succ-pow-tendsto">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.charFun_centered_standardized_uniformOn_univ_inv_sqrt_succ_pow_tendsto</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Gaussian characteristic-function power limit for a standardized centered
empirical one-draw law with fixed support.</p>
<p>This is the fixed-support analytic bridge behind the characteristic-function

                (fun i =&gt;
                  instHDiv.hDiv (instHSub.hSub (Y i) (HansenEconometrics.empiricalMean Y))
                    (ProbabilityTheory.variance Y (ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn Set.univ)).sqrt)
                (ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn Set.univ))

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 10.2, second conclusion from the centered bootstrap WLLN.</p>
<p>Once the centered bootstrap sample mean satisfies
<code>Ybar* - Ybar -&gt;p* 0</code>, and the ordinary sample mean satisfies
<code>Ybar -&gt;p μY</code>, the bootstrap sample mean itself satisfies
<code>Ybar* -&gt;p* μY</code>.  This is the bootstrap Slutsky/addition step used in the
textbook proof after the centered WLLN is established by the conditional
variance bound. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {Ωs : Type u_2} {E : Type u_4} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {mΩs : MeasurableSpace Ωs}

  (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω), MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (Pstar n ω)) →
    ∀ {YbarStar : Nat → Ω → Ωs → E} {Ybar : Nat → Ω → E} {μY : E},
      (HansenEconometrics.TendstoInBootstrapProbability μ Pstar
          (fun n ω ωs =&gt; instHSub.hSub (YbarStar n ω ωs) (Ybar n ω)) fun x =&gt; 0) →
        (MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ Ybar Filter.atTop fun x =&gt; μY) →
          HansenEconometrics.TendstoInBootstrapProbability μ Pstar YbarStar fun x =&gt; μY</code></pre>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-10-4">
<summary><span>Theorem 10.4</span><span class="result-count">6 of 49 linked endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>Bootstrap CLT. If <code>Y_i</code> are i.i.d., <code>E ‖Y‖^2 &lt; ∞</code>, and <code>Σ = Var[Y] &gt; 0</code>, then the normalized bootstrap sample mean converges in bootstrap distribution to <code>N(0,Σ)</code></p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-chapter10-bootstrap-clt-gaussian-of-tendsto-cdf">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.chapter10_bootstrap_clt_gaussian_of_tendsto_cdf</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 10.4, Gaussian bootstrap CLT CDF wrapper.</p>
<p>If the conditional CDFs of a normalized bootstrap statistic converge in
probability to the CDF of <code>N(0, Σ)</code> at every continuity point, then the
statistic converges in bootstrap distribution to that Gaussian law. Later
ordinary-bootstrap wrappers discharge this premise through pathwise weak
convergence, scalar projection/characteristic-function routes, and the iid
covariance-tail route. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {Ωs : Type u_2} {k : Type u_6} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {mΩs : MeasurableSpace Ωs}
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst : Fintype k] [inst_1 : DecidableEq k] {Pstar : Nat → Ω → MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs}
  {Zstar : Nat → Ω → Ωs → k → Real} {S : Matrix k k Real},
  (∀ (x : k → Real),
      ContinuousAt
          (fun y =&gt; HansenEconometrics.vectorCDF (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 S) (fun z =&gt; z.ofLp) y) x →
        MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ (fun n ω =&gt; HansenEconometrics.bootstrapVectorCDF Pstar Zstar x n ω)
          Filter.atTop fun x_1 =&gt;
          HansenEconometrics.vectorCDF (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 S) (fun z =&gt; z.ofLp) x) →
    HansenEconometrics.TendstoInBootstrapDistribution μ Pstar Zstar (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 S)
      fun z =&gt; z.ofLp</code></pre>
</details>

convergence.</p>
<p>If a normalized bootstrap statistic converges weakly, in the
bounded-continuous-test-function bootstrap sense, to <code>N(0, S)</code>, then the
coordinate-CDF version of Hansen Definition 10.2 follows at all continuity

<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 10.5, globally continuous event-probability face.</p>
<p>After a continuous transformation <code>g</code>, bounded-continuous lower/upper
sandwiches for an event <code>A</code> imply convergence in probability of the conditional
bootstrap event probabilities.  The remaining textbook discontinuity-set-null
case supplies these sandwiches from the null-boundary hypothesis. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {Ωs : Type u_2} {Ωlim : Type u_3} {E : Type u_4} {F : Type u_5} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
  {mΩs : MeasurableSpace Ωs} {mΩlim : MeasurableSpace Ωlim} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure Ωlim} [inst : TopologicalSpace E] [inst_1 : TopologicalSpace F]
  {Pstar : Nat → Ω → MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs} {Zstar : Nat → Ω → Ωs → E} {Z : Ωlim → E} {g : E → F} {A : Set F}
  {c : Real},
  HansenEconometrics.TendstoInBootstrapWeakDistribution μ Pstar Zstar ν Z →
    Continuous g →
      (∀ (ε : Real),
          Real.instLT.lt 0 ε →
            Exists fun lower =&gt;
              Exists fun upper =&gt;
                And
                  (Real.instLE.le
                    (MeasureTheory.integral ν fun ωlim =&gt; BoundedContinuousFunction.instFunLike.coe lower (g (Z ωlim)))
                    c)
                  (And
                    (Real.instLE.le c
                      (MeasureTheory.integral ν fun ωlim =&gt;
                        BoundedContinuousFunction.instFunLike.coe upper (g (Z ωlim))))
                    (And
                      (Real.instLE.le
                        (instHSub.hSub
                          (MeasureTheory.integral ν fun ωlim =&gt;
                            BoundedContinuousFunction.instFunLike.coe upper (g (Z ωlim)))
                          (MeasureTheory.integral ν fun ωlim =&gt;
                            BoundedContinuousFunction.instFunLike.coe lower (g (Z ωlim))))
                        ε)
                      (And
                        (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω),
                          Real.instLE.le
                            (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapBoundedContinuousIntegral Pstar
                              (fun n ω ωs =&gt; g (Zstar n ω ωs)) lower n ω)
                            (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapEventProbability Pstar (fun n ω ωs =&gt; g (Zstar n ω ωs)) A n ω))
                        (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω),
                          Real.instLE.le
                            (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapEventProbability Pstar (fun n ω ωs =&gt; g (Zstar n ω ωs)) A n ω)
                            (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapBoundedContinuousIntegral Pstar
                              (fun n ω ωs =&gt; g (Zstar n ω ωs)) upper n ω)))))) →
        MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ
          (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapEventProbability Pstar (fun n ω ωs =&gt; g (Zstar n ω ωs)) A) Filter.atTop fun x =&gt;
          c</code></pre>

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 10.6, Gaussian covariance specialization.</p>
<p>If the bootstrap linearized statistic converges weakly to <code>N(0, V)</code>, then its
matrix-derivative image converges weakly to <code>N(0, G V G')</code>, matching the
textbook covariance formula. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>

  [inst_3 : DecidableEq r] {Pstar : Nat → Ω → MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs} {Tstar : Nat → Ω → Ωs → EuclideanSpace Real d}
  {V : Matrix d d Real} (G : Matrix r d Real),
  V.PosSemidef →
    (HansenEconometrics.TendstoInBootstrapWeakDistribution μ Pstar Tstar (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 V)
        fun z =&gt; z) →
      HansenEconometrics.TendstoInBootstrapWeakDistribution μ Pstar

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-10-9">
<summary><span>Theorem 10.9</span><span class="result-count">6 of 22 linked endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If the normalized statistic and its bootstrap analogue have the same limit law and the bootstrap statistic is uniformly square integrable, then finite-replication bootstrap variance converges to the conditional bootstrap variance and the conditional bootstrap variance converges to the asymptotic variance</p></div>

<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 10.9 finite-dimensional mean-vector wrapper.</p>
<p>Bootstrap weak convergence of the vector statistic plus the named
uniform-square-tail condition on each coordinate implies convergence in
probability of the conditional bootstrap mean vector.  This is the
coordinatewise vector surface used by the covariance and trimmed-variance
layers, where the textbook proofs first establish scalar uniform
square-integrability for every coordinate. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {Ωs : Type u_2} {Ωlim : Type u_3} {k : Type u_6} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {mΩs : MeasurableSpace Ωs}
  {mΩlim : MeasurableSpace Ωlim} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure Ωlim} [inst : Fintype k]
  [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν] {Pstar : Nat → Ω → MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs} {Zstar : Nat → Ω → Ωs → k → Real}
  {Z : Ωlim → k → Real},
  (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω), MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (Pstar n ω)) →
    (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω) (a : k), MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun ωs =&gt; Zstar n ω ωs a) 2 (Pstar n ω)) →
      (∀ (a : k), MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun ωlim =&gt; Z ωlim a) 2 ν) →
        HansenEconometrics.TendstoInBootstrapWeakDistribution μ Pstar Zstar ν Z →
          (∀ (a : k),
              HansenEconometrics.BootstrapUniformSquareTail μ Pstar (fun n ω ωs =&gt; Zstar n ω ωs a) ν fun ωlim =&gt;
                Z ωlim a) →
            MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapMeanVec Pstar Zstar) Filter.atTop fun x a =&gt;
              MeasureTheory.integral ν fun ωlim =&gt; Z ωlim a</code></pre>

<p>This packages the two variance layers used in the theorem: a finite-replication
simulation-error premise estimates the conditional bootstrap variance, while
bootstrap weak convergence plus the named uniform-square-tail condition sends
that conditional variance to the limiting variance functional. </p></div>

<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {Ωs : Type u_2} {Ωlim : Type u_3} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {mΩs : MeasurableSpace Ωs}

                Filter.atTop fun x =&gt;

square-tail conditions rather than developing a separate product-tail API. </p></div>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-10-9-ordinary-nonparametric-scalar-variance-support">
<summary><span>Theorem 10.9 ordinary nonparametric scalar variance support</span><span class="result-count">6 endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>The normalized ordinary <code>Fin (n+1)</code> bootstrap mean has conditional variance converging to the population variance once the empirical one-draw variance converges; iid finite-second-moment assumptions discharge that empirical variance premise</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-variance-uniformon-finsucc-tendsto-of-mean-second-moments">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.variance_uniformOn_finSucc_tendsto_of_mean_second_moments</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Empirical scalar variance convergence from empirical first and second
moments.</p>
<p>This is the scalar counterpart of
<code>covMat_uniformOn_finSucc_tendsto_of_mean_cross_moments</code>: once the empirical
mean and raw second moment on <code>Fin (n+1)</code> converge, the finite empirical
variance converges to the population variance. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  (Y : Nat → Ω → Real),
  MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun ω =&gt; Y 0 ω) 2 μ →
    (MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ
        (fun n ω =&gt; MeasureTheory.integral (ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn Set.univ) fun i =&gt; Y i.val ω) Filter.atTop
        fun x =&gt; MeasureTheory.integral μ fun ω =&gt; Y 0 ω) →
      (MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ
          (fun n ω =&gt;
            MeasureTheory.integral (ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn Set.univ) fun i =&gt; instHPow.hPow (Y i.val ω) 2)
          Filter.atTop fun x =&gt; MeasureTheory.integral μ fun ω =&gt; instHPow.hPow (Y 0 ω) 2) →

convergence.</p>

reduces the bootstrap conditional variance to the finite empirical variance. </p></div>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-10-9-10-11-ordinary-nonparametric-finite-replication-scalar-variance-support">
<summary><span>Theorem 10.9/10.11 ordinary nonparametric finite-replication scalar variance support</span><span class="result-count">6 endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>The normalized ordinary <code>Fin (n+1)</code> bootstrap variance can feed moment-form and Hansen-centered finite-replication scalar variance estimators</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-chapter10-indexed-finitereplicationvariance-finsucc-l2-iid">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.chapter10_indexed_finiteReplicationVariance_finSucc_l2_iid</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Theorem 10.9/10.11 ordinary nonparametric-bootstrap finite-replication
scalar variance route for iid observations.</p>
<p>The conditional variance target is the normalized <code>Fin (n+1)</code> ordinary
bootstrap variance.  Coordinatewise <code>O(n⁻¹)</code> mean-square simulation error
transfers the moment-form finite-replication variance estimator to the
population variance target. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  {Zsim : Nat → Nat → Ω → Real} {Cfinite : Real} (Y : Nat → Ω → Real),
  MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun ω =&gt; Y 0 ω) 2 μ →
    Pairwise (Function.onFun (fun x1 x2 =&gt; ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun x1 x2 μ) Y) →
      (∀ (i : Nat), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (Y i) (Y 0) μ μ) →
        (∀ (n : Nat),
            MeasureTheory.Integrable
              (fun ω =&gt;
                instHPow.hPow
                  (Real.norm.norm
                    (instHSub.hSub (HansenEconometrics.finiteReplicationVarianceMomentReal Zsim n ω)
                      (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapVarianceRealIndexed (fun n x =&gt; ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn Set.univ)
                        (fun n ω ωs =&gt;
                          instHMul.hMul (instHAdd.hAdd n.cast 1).sqrt
                            (instHSub.hSub
                              (HansenEconometrics.empiricalBootstrapResampleMean (fun i =&gt; Y i.val ω) (fun ωs t =&gt; ωs t)
                                ωs)
                              (HansenEconometrics.empiricalMean fun i =&gt; Y i.val ω)))
                        n ω)))
                  2)
              μ) →
          Filter.Eventually
              (fun n =&gt;
                Real.instLE.le
                  (MeasureTheory.integral μ fun ω =&gt;
                    instHPow.hPow
                      (Real.norm.norm
                        (instHSub.hSub (HansenEconometrics.finiteReplicationVarianceMomentReal Zsim n ω)
                          (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapVarianceRealIndexed
                            (fun n x =&gt; ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn Set.univ)
                            (fun n ω ωs =&gt;
                              instHMul.hMul (instHAdd.hAdd n.cast 1).sqrt
                                (instHSub.hSub
                                  (HansenEconometrics.empiricalBootstrapResampleMean (fun i =&gt; Y i.val ω)
                                    (fun ωs t =&gt; ωs t) ωs)
                                  (HansenEconometrics.empiricalMean fun i =&gt; Y i.val ω)))
                            n ω)))
                      2)
                  (instHDiv.hDiv Cfinite n.cast))
              Filter.atTop →
            MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ (HansenEconometrics.finiteReplicationVarianceMomentReal Zsim) Filter.atTop
              fun x =&gt; ProbabilityTheory.variance (fun ω =&gt; Y 0 ω) μ</code></pre>
</details>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-chapter10-finitereplicationvariance-tendsto-of-moments">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.chapter10_finiteReplicationVariance_tendsto_of_moments</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 10.11, finite-replication variance moment bridge.</p>
<p>If the finite-<code>B</code> replication mean and second moment converge in probability to
their conditional limits, then the moment-form finite-replication variance
converges in probability to <code>m₂ - m²</code>.  In applications, the moment premises are
the bootstrap WLLN for bounded trimmed replications. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {Z : Nat → Nat → Ω → Real} {m m₂ : Real},
  (MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ (HansenEconometrics.finiteReplicationMeanReal Z) Filter.atTop fun x =&gt; m) →
    (MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ (HansenEconometrics.finiteReplicationSecondMomentReal Z) Filter.atTop fun x =&gt;
        m₂) →
      MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ (HansenEconometrics.finiteReplicationVarianceMomentReal Z) Filter.atTop fun x =&gt;
        instHSub.hSub m₂ (instHPow.hPow m 2)</code></pre>
</details>

<div class="textbook-statement"><p>Under the assumptions of Theorem 10.7, the trimmed conditional bootstrap variance <code>V̂^boot,τ_θ = Var*(Z**_n)</code> converges to the asymptotic variance <code>V_θ</code></p></div>

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 10.12, trimmed conditional covariance moment bridge.</p>
<p>For the trimmed statistic <code>Z** = Z* 1{‖Z*‖ ≤ τ}</code>, convergence of its conditional
mean vector and cross-moment matrix implies convergence of its conditional
covariance matrix.  The smooth-model proof of Theorem 10.12 supplies these
moment premises by showing the trimming is asymptotically negligible and the
trimmed sequence is uniformly square integrable. </p></div>

    (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω) (a : k),

      ∀ {m : k → Real} {M₂ : Matrix k k Real},
        (MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ
            (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapMeanVec Pstar (HansenEconometrics.trimmedBootstrapStatistic Zstar τ))
            Filter.atTop fun x =&gt; m) →
          (MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ
              (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapCrossMomentMat Pstar (HansenEconometrics.trimmedBootstrapStatistic Zstar τ))
              Filter.atTop fun x =&gt; M₂) →
            MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ (HansenEconometrics.trimmedBootstrapCovarianceMat Pstar Zstar τ)
              Filter.atTop fun x a c =&gt; instHSub.hSub (M₂ a c) (instHMul.hMul (m a) (m c))</code></pre>

<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 10.9 finite-dimensional mean-vector wrapper.</p>
<p>Bootstrap weak convergence of the vector statistic plus the named
uniform-square-tail condition on each coordinate implies convergence in
probability of the conditional bootstrap mean vector.  This is the
coordinatewise vector surface used by the covariance and trimmed-variance
layers, where the textbook proofs first establish scalar uniform
square-integrability for every coordinate. </p></div>

  {Z : Ωlim → k → Real},
  (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω), MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (Pstar n ω)) →
    (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω) (a : k), MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun ωs =&gt; Zstar n ω ωs a) 2 (Pstar n ω)) →
      (∀ (a : k), MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun ωlim =&gt; Z ωlim a) 2 ν) →
        HansenEconometrics.TendstoInBootstrapWeakDistribution μ Pstar Zstar ν Z →
          (∀ (a : k),
              HansenEconometrics.BootstrapUniformSquareTail μ Pstar (fun n ω ωs =&gt; Zstar n ω ωs a) ν fun ωlim =&gt;
                Z ωlim a) →

              MeasureTheory.integral ν fun ωlim =&gt; Z ωlim a</code></pre>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-tendstoinbootstrapweakdistribution">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">def</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.TendstoInBootstrapWeakDistribution</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Bootstrap convergence in distribution in bounded-continuous-test-function
form.</p>
<p>For every bounded continuous real test function, the conditional bootstrap
expectation converges in ordinary probability to the corresponding expectation
under the limiting law. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">{Ω : Type u_1} →
  {Ωs : Type u_2} →
    {Ωlim : Type u_3} →
      {E : Type u_4} →
        {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} →
          {mΩs : MeasurableSpace Ωs} →
            {mΩlim : MeasurableSpace Ωlim} →
              [TopologicalSpace E] →
                MeasureTheory.Measure Ω →
                  (Nat → Ω → MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs) →
                    (Nat → Ω → Ωs → E) → MeasureTheory.Measure Ωlim → (Ωlim → E) → Prop</code></pre>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-tendstoinbootstrapdistribution">

<p>The conditional CDF of <code>Zstar n</code> converges in ordinary probability, under the
original-sample law <code>μ</code>, to the limit CDF at every continuity point of the

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-chapter10-bootstrap-variance-consistency-of-weak-distribution-uniform-square-tail">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.chapter10_bootstrap_variance_consistency_of_weak_distribution_uniform_square_tail</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 10.9, weak-distribution plus uniform-square-tail variance
bridge.</p>
<p>This is the theorem-facing uniform-integrability assembly: for every tolerance
one chooses a large threshold whose squared tail is small for the limit law and
small in probability for the conditional bootstrap law. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {Ωs : Type u_2} {Ωlim : Type u_3} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {mΩs : MeasurableSpace Ωs}
  {mΩlim : MeasurableSpace Ωlim} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure Ωlim}
  [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν] {Pstar : Nat → Ω → MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs} {Zstar : Nat → Ω → Ωs → Real}
  {Z : Ωlim → Real},
  (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω), MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (Pstar n ω)) →
    (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω), MeasureTheory.MemLp (Zstar n ω) 2 (Pstar n ω)) →
      MeasureTheory.MemLp Z 2 ν →
        HansenEconometrics.TendstoInBootstrapWeakDistribution μ Pstar Zstar ν Z →
          (∀ (ε : Real),
              Real.instLT.lt 0 ε →
                Exists fun R =&gt;
                  And (Real.instLE.le 1 R)
                    (And
                      (Real.instLE.le
                        (MeasureTheory.integral ν fun ωlim =&gt;
                          (setOf fun ωlim =&gt; Real.instLE.le R (abs (Z ωlim))).indicator
                            (fun ωlim =&gt; instHPow.hPow (Z ωlim) 2) ωlim)
                        ε)
                      (Filter.Tendsto
                        (fun n =&gt;
                          MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe μ
                            (setOf fun ω =&gt;
                              Real.instLE.le ε
                                (Real.pseudoMetricSpace.dist
                                  (MeasureTheory.integral (Pstar n ω) fun ωs =&gt;
                                    (setOf fun ωs =&gt; Real.instLE.le R (abs (Zstar n ω ωs))).indicator
                                      (fun ωs =&gt; instHPow.hPow (Zstar n ω ωs) 2) ωs)
                                  0)))
                        Filter.atTop (nhds 0)))) →
            MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapVarianceReal Pstar Zstar) Filter.atTop
              fun x =&gt;
              instHSub.hSub (MeasureTheory.integral ν fun ωlim =&gt; instHPow.hPow (Z ωlim) 2)
                (instHPow.hPow (MeasureTheory.integral ν fun ωlim =&gt; Z ωlim) 2)</code></pre>
</details>
<details class="dependency-list"><summary>Direct statement dependencies (2)</summary><ul><li><code>HansenEconometrics.TendstoInBootstrapWeakDistribution</code></li><li><code>HansenEconometrics.bootstrapVarianceReal</code></li></ul></details>
<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/Chapter10Bootstrap/Variance.lean#L4300">HansenEconometrics/Chapter10Bootstrap/Variance.lean:4300</a></p>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-chapter10-finitereplicationvariance-tendsto-of-weak-distribution-uniformsquaretail">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.chapter10_finiteReplicationVariance_tendsto_of_weak_distribution_uniformSquareTail</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 10.9/10.11 finite-replication variance from bootstrap weak
convergence and a uniform-square-tail condition.</p>
<p>This packages the two variance layers used in the theorem: a finite-replication
simulation-error premise estimates the conditional bootstrap variance, while
bootstrap weak convergence plus the named uniform-square-tail condition sends
that conditional variance to the limiting variance functional. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {Ωs : Type u_2} {Ωlim : Type u_3} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {mΩs : MeasurableSpace Ωs}
  {mΩlim : MeasurableSpace Ωlim} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure Ωlim}
  [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν] {Zsim : Nat → Nat → Ω → Real} {Pstar : Nat → Ω → MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs}
  {Zstar : Nat → Ω → Ωs → Real} {Z : Ωlim → Real},
  (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω), MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (Pstar n ω)) →
    (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω), MeasureTheory.MemLp (Zstar n ω) 2 (Pstar n ω)) →
      MeasureTheory.MemLp Z 2 ν →
        HansenEconometrics.TendstoInBootstrapWeakDistribution μ Pstar Zstar ν Z →
          HansenEconometrics.BootstrapUniformSquareTail μ Pstar Zstar ν Z →
            (MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ
                (fun n ω =&gt;
                  instHSub.hSub (HansenEconometrics.finiteReplicationVarianceMomentReal Zsim n ω)
                    (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapVarianceReal Pstar Zstar n ω))
                Filter.atTop fun x =&gt; 0) →
              MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ (HansenEconometrics.finiteReplicationVarianceMomentReal Zsim)
                Filter.atTop fun x =&gt;
                instHSub.hSub (MeasureTheory.integral ν fun ωlim =&gt; instHPow.hPow (Z ωlim) 2)
                  (instHPow.hPow (MeasureTheory.integral ν fun ωlim =&gt; Z ωlim) 2)</code></pre>
</details>

<details class="result-group" id="equation-10-17">
<summary><span>Equation 10.17</span><span class="result-count">6 endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>The fourth conditional moment of the normalized bootstrap sample mean is <code>O_p(1)</code>, giving uniform square integrability</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-bootstrapuniformsquaretail-of-fourthmoment-tendstoinmeasure">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.bootstrapUniformSquareTail_of_fourthMoment_tendstoInMeasure</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Uniform square-tail constructor from a fourth-moment convergence premise.</p>
<p>The conditional fourth moment controls the conditional squared tail by

bootstrap quantile limits and symmetry identity for the limit law. </p></div>

<div class="declaration-body">

masses <code>alpha / 2</code> and <code>1 - alpha / 2</code>, then the ideal BC interval has
coverage <code>1 - alpha</code>. </p></div>

  {psi : Real → Real} {theta z0 zLower zUpper alpha : Real} {thetaHat : Ω → Real},
  ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw (fun ω =&gt; HansenEconometrics.biasCorrectedPivot psi theta z0 (thetaHat ω)) eta μ →
    Real.instLE.le zLower zUpper →
      Eq ((ProbabilityTheory.cdf eta).toFun (Real.instNeg.neg zUpper)) (instHDiv.hDiv alpha 2) →
        Eq ((ProbabilityTheory.cdf eta).toFun (Real.instNeg.neg zLower)) (instHSub.hSub 1 (instHDiv.hDiv alpha 2)) →
          Eq
            (MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe μ
              (setOf fun ω =&gt; HansenEconometrics.biasCorrectedIdealCIEvent psi theta (thetaHat ω) z0 zLower zUpper))
            (ENNReal.ofReal (instHSub.hSub 1 alpha))</code></pre>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-chapter10-percentiletci-coverage-tendsto-of-joint-quantile-limit">

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 10.14, percentile-<code>t</code> interval coverage bridge.</p>
<p>If the sample t-ratio and bootstrap percentile-<code>t</code> critical values jointly
converge to <code>(ξ, qL, qU)</code>, and the limiting coverage boundary has zero
probability, then percentile-<code>t</code> interval coverage converges to
<code>P[qL &lt;= ξ &lt;= qU]</code>. Hansen's first-order validity conclusion <code>1 - α</code> is
obtained by instantiating this bridge with the bootstrap quantile limits from
(10.31). </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {Ωlim : Type u_3} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {mΩlim : MeasurableSpace Ωlim} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure Ωlim} [inst : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν] {θ : Real} {θhat se qLower qUpper : Nat → Ω → Real} {ξ : Ωlim → Real}
  {qLowerLim qUpperLim : Real},
  (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω), Real.instLT.lt 0 (se n ω)) →
    MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution (HansenEconometrics.percentileTCoverageVector θ θhat se qLower qUpper)
        Filter.atTop (HansenEconometrics.percentileTCoverageLimitVector ξ qLowerLim qUpperLim) (fun x =&gt; μ) ν →
      Eq
          (MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe
            (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (HansenEconometrics.percentileTCoverageLimitVector ξ qLowerLim qUpperLim) ν)
            (frontier HansenEconometrics.percentileTCoverageSet))
          0 →
        Filter.Tendsto
          (fun n =&gt;
            MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe μ
              (setOf fun ω =&gt; HansenEconometrics.percentileTCIEvent θ (θhat n ω) (se n ω) (qLower n ω) (qUpper n ω)))
          Filter.atTop
          (nhds
            (MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe
              (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (HansenEconometrics.percentileTCoverageLimitVector ξ qLowerLim qUpperLim) ν)
              HansenEconometrics.percentileTCoverageSet))</code></pre>
</details>

        Real.instLT.lt 0 seθ →

            (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω), MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (Pstar n ω)) →

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-10-15">
<summary><span>Theorem 10.15</span><span class="result-count">6 of 12 linked endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>Under the assumptions of Theorem 9.11, the percentile-<code>t</code> interval has higher-order coverage <code>P[θ ∈ C_pt] = 1 - α + O(n^{-1})</code></p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-chapter10-percentilet-secondorder-interval-expansion">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.chapter10_percentileT_secondOrder_interval_expansion</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 10.15, Edgeworth component of the percentile-<code>t</code> refinement.</p>
<p>A second-order Edgeworth expansion for a scalar t-ratio gives the symmetric
interval probability expansion used by the percentile-<code>t</code> bootstrap interval.
The even <code>p₁</code> and odd <code>p₂</code> hypotheses encode the cancellation of the
<code>n^{-1/2}</code> Edgeworth term in two-sided intervals. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  {T : Nat → Ω → Real} {baseCDF density p1 p2 : Real → Real} {c coverage : Real},
  HansenEconometrics.SecondOrderEdgeworthExpansion μ T baseCDF density p1 p2 →
    Eq (p1 (Real.instNeg.neg c)) (p1 c) →
      Eq (p2 (Real.instNeg.neg c)) (Real.instNeg.neg (p2 c)) →
        Eq (density (Real.instNeg.neg c)) (density c) →
          Eq (instHSub.hSub (baseCDF c) (baseCDF (Real.instNeg.neg c))) coverage →
            Filter.Tendsto
              (fun n =&gt;
                instHMul.hMul n.cast
                  (instHSub.hSub
                    (instHSub.hSub
                      (instHSub.hSub (HansenEconometrics.statisticCDFReal μ T n c)
                        (HansenEconometrics.statisticCDFReal μ T n (Real.instNeg.neg c)))
                      coverage)
                    (instHMul.hMul (Real.instInv.inv n.cast) (instHMul.hMul 2 (instHMul.hMul (p2 c) (density c))))))
              Filter.atTop (nhds 0)</code></pre>
</details>

<div class="result-body">

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Two-sided bootstrap-test calibration from a bootstrap distribution whose
absolute-statistic scalar limit has law <code>ηAbs</code>.</p>
<p>The absolute bootstrap statistic may converge on an auxiliary probability
space; <code>HasLaw</code> identifies its scalar CDF for the lower critical-value
quantile route. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {Ωs : Type u_2} {Ωlim : Type u_3} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {mΩs : MeasurableSpace Ωs}
  {mΩlim : MeasurableSpace Ωlim} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure Ωlim}
  [inst : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν] {Ωstar : Type u_7}
  [inst_2 : MeasurableSpace Ωstar] {η ηAbs : MeasureTheory.Measure Real} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure η]
  [MeasureTheory.NoAtoms η] [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ηAbs] {νstar : MeasureTheory.Measure Ωstar}
  {Alim : Ωstar → Real} {Pstar : Nat → Ω → MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs} {Astar : Nat → Ω → Ωs → Real} {T : Nat → Ω → Real}
  {ξ : Ωlim → Real} {critLim α : Real},
  MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution T Filter.atTop ξ (fun x =&gt; μ) ν →
    (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω), MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (Pstar n ω)) →
      (∀ (n : Nat) (ω : Ω), AEMeasurable (Astar n ω) (Pstar n ω)) →
        Real.instLT.lt 0 α →
          Real.instLT.lt α 1 →
            (StrictMono fun x =&gt; (ProbabilityTheory.cdf ηAbs).toFun x) →
              Eq ((ProbabilityTheory.cdf ηAbs).toFun critLim) (instHSub.hSub 1 α) →
                (HansenEconometrics.TendstoInBootstrapDistribution μ Pstar (fun n ω ωs x =&gt; Astar n ω ωs) νstar
                    fun ωstar x =&gt; Alim ωstar) →
                  ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw Alim ηAbs νstar →
                    (∀ (x : Real), ContinuousAt (fun y =&gt; (ProbabilityTheory.cdf ηAbs).toFun y) x) →
                      (∀ (n : Nat),
                          AEMeasurable
                            (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapScalarLowerQuantile Pstar Astar (instHSub.hSub 1 α) n) μ) →
                        ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw ξ η ν →
                          Real.instLE.le 0 critLim →
                            Eq ((ProbabilityTheory.cdf η).toFun (Real.instNeg.neg critLim)) (instHDiv.hDiv α 2) →
                              Eq ((ProbabilityTheory.cdf η).toFun critLim) (instHSub.hSub 1 (instHDiv.hDiv α 2)) →
                                Filter.Tendsto
                                  (fun n =&gt;
                                    MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe μ
                                      (setOf fun ω =&gt;
                                        HansenEconometrics.bootstrapAbsTestReject (T n ω)
                                          (HansenEconometrics.bootstrapScalarLowerQuantile Pstar Astar
                                            (instHSub.hSub 1 α) n ω)))
                                  Filter.atTop (nhds (ENNReal.ofReal α))</code></pre>

The bootstrap-quantile step of Theorem 10.17 supplies the additional
critical-value transfer premise needed to turn this fixed-critical expansion
into the <code>o(n^{-1})</code> bootstrap-test refinement. </p></div>

<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>Under Assumption 7.2, the bootstrap regression estimator has the same Gaussian limit as the sample estimator; under Assumption 7.3 the transformed statistic has covariance <code>V_θ = R' V_β R</code>; under Assumption 7.4 the bootstrap t-statistic is standard normal</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-chapter10-bootstrap-regression-theta-gaussian">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.chapter10_bootstrap_regression_theta_gaussian</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 10.18, nonlinear-regression delta-method Gaussian wrapper.</p>
<p>If the bootstrap regression coefficient statistic converges weakly to
<code>N(0,Vβ)</code>, then the derivative-linearized statistic for a smooth transformation
with Jacobian <code>R</code> converges weakly to <code>N(0,R' Vβ R)</code>.  This is the regression
surface of the bootstrap Delta method; the concrete OLS bootstrap constructor
supplies the coefficient-level bootstrap CLT premise. </p></div>

  [inst_3 : DecidableEq q] {Pstar : Nat → Ω → MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs}
  {TbetaStar : Nat → Ω → Ωs → EuclideanSpace Real k} {Vβ : Matrix k k Real} (R : Matrix k q Real),
  Vβ.PosSemidef →
    (HansenEconometrics.TendstoInBootstrapWeakDistribution μ Pstar TbetaStar
        (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 Vβ) fun z =&gt; z) →
      HansenEconometrics.TendstoInBootstrapWeakDistribution μ Pstar
        (fun n ω ωs =&gt;
          ContinuousLinearMap.funLike.coe (HansenEconometrics.matrixContinuousLinearMap R.transpose) (TbetaStar n ω ωs))
        (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0
          (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul
            (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul R.transpose Vβ) R))

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-chapter10-bootstrap-regression-tstat-standardnormal">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.chapter10_bootstrap_regression_tstat_standardNormal</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 10.18, regression bootstrap t-statistic standard-normal
wrapper.</p>
<p>If the transformed regression numerator and feasible standard-error scale have
joint bootstrap weak limit <code>(s Z, s)</code> with <code>Z ~ N(0,1)</code>, and the scale itself
converges to the positive constant <code>s</code> in bootstrap probability, then the
studentized transformed statistic has standard-normal bootstrap weak limit.
Concrete regression applications supply the joint numerator/scale limit and
scale consistency from the model-specific covariance estimator. </p></div>

<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 10.19, regression-facing trimmed bootstrap variance bridge.</p>
<p>For the transformed regression statistic, if the trimmed conditional mean
converges to zero and the trimmed conditional cross moment converges to the
delta-method covariance <code>R' Vβ R</code>, then the trimmed bootstrap covariance
estimator converges to <code>R' Vβ R</code>.  The concrete regression proof supplies these
moment premises from Theorems 10.11 and 10.12. </p></div>
